primer.title: A reference must not outlive what it points to
body: Every reference has a lifetime: the stretch of code in which the value it points to is guaranteed to exist. Usually the compiler infers it (*elision*).

Elision gives up when a function returns a reference and takes **several** reference parameters: it cannot tell which one the result borrows from. `'a` on the parameters and the result says "the result lives no longer than these".
Annotations never change how long anything lives. They only describe a relationship, which the compiler then checks at each call site.
A struct that stores a reference needs a lifetime parameter too: `struct Book<'a> { title: &'a str }` — a `Book` may not outlive the text it points into.

options.text: E0106: the return type on line 1 needs a lifetime — the compiler cannot tell whether the result borrows from `x` or `y`
options.rationale: With two reference parameters, elision has no rule to pick one. `fn longest<'a>(x: &'a str, y: &'a str) -> &'a str` states the relationship.

options.text: E0515: `longest` returns a reference to a local variable
options.rationale: `x` and `y` are borrowed from the caller, not created inside the function. Returning them is sound — it just is not *described* yet.
It would, with the lifetime added. The body is fine; only the signature is incomplete.

exercises.rationale: Line 14 borrows `string2`, and because of `'a` the result may point into it. `string2` is dropped on line 15, but `result` is still used on line 16 (E0597: borrowed value does not live long enough).

lineRationales.15: This is where `string2` is dropped — the compiler mentions this line in a note, but it reports the error at the borrow on line 14.
lineRationales.16: This use is what forces the borrow to last past line 15. The compiler points at it in a note; the error itself is on line 14.
lineRationales.1: The signature is correct. It is precisely what tells the compiler that `result` might borrow from `string2`.
lineRationales.11: Declaring a variable without a value is fine as long as it is assigned before use.

exercises.fallbackRationale: That line compiles. Find the value with the shortest life, then the borrow of it that escapes.

lineRationales.8: String literals are `&'static str`, valid forever. The values are fine; the struct definition is incomplete.

options.rationale: A block is an expression; its value is its last expression without a semicolon.
